A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, figures, and complete appendices. Reordered proofs and relocated experiments can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figures 1–4 report original simulations of ST, Lasso, and ridge regression, including stability rates and distributions of standardized CV errors.

after.justification: The original simulations remain in Figures 2–5, including Appendix M. Figure 1 additionally reports simulated Lasso confidence-interval coverage.

M1.justification: The ST, Lasso, ridge, CV inference, and conservative comparison-interval procedures are retained. Formalizing the Lasso objective and its proximity to ST adds analysis without changing these algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gaussian linear-regression setting with sparse and fully dense ten-dimensional coefficient vectors. The added coverage plot uses the existing sparse population and task.

E2.justification: ST, Lasso, and ridge retain their participation in the corresponding experiments. The new Lasso coverage plot introduces no additional comparison method.

E3.justification: Figure 1 and Appendix B add a fixed-penalty Lasso coverage evaluation with lambda_n = sqrt(n), delta_n = 1, the largest retained sample size, true variance, and nominal coverage swept across its full range. Existing experiments retain their sample sizes, ten-fold CV, and tuning procedures.

E4.justification: Figure 1 adds a direct actual-versus-nominal coverage diagnostic, supplementing the earlier stability-rate and distributional checks. The ridge and dense-signal ST analyses remain unchanged and move to Appendix M.

E5.justification: Both versions report 50,000 CV replications, 5,000,000 or 1,000,000 Monte Carlo replications depending on penalty selection, seed initialization, and the same two-standard-error bands and delta-method calculation. No new uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: New Figure 1 reports near-nominal coverage for individual Lasso assessment and substantial undercoverage for Lasso comparisons under its fixed-penalty protocol. The numerical annotations and trends in v1 Figures 1–4 are retained in v2 Figures 2–5.

T1.justification: v2 adds Lasso–ST proximity Lemma 2.3, Lasso instability and stability Theorems 3.3–3.4, and their proofs in Appendices C, J, and K. It also derives truncated-normal moments in Lemma H.3 and corrects the union-bound sign in Proposition 6.1. The original ST theorems and most supporting proofs are retained.

C1.justification: v1 presents formal results for ST and empirical confirmation for Lasso. v2 promotes individual Lasso stability and Lasso comparison instability to central theoretical contributions in the abstract, introduction, and main results.

C2.justification: v2 explains why favorable assumptions make the instability counterexample consequential and explicitly limits generalization beyond the studied distributions and models. Section 6 also clarifies that experiments demonstrate CV failure rather than establish the best inference procedure; the existing stable examples and open necessity question remain.

D1.justification: Section 5 replaces the generic supplemental-code statement with a specific repository address, and Appendix B documents the new coverage experiment. Existing library, grid-search, sample-size, and replication details remain available in the renamed Appendix L.

R1.justification: v2 adds distinctions from Luo and Barber's expected-test-error inference and Xu et al.'s uniform-instability results for sparse algorithms. It adds supporting and application references and replaces truncated-normal sources while retaining the original CV and stability positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, the theoretical narrative now leads with comparison instability, and penalty-regime discussion is repositioned. The conclusion is substantially expanded, appendix proofs are reordered, and the comparison-variance proof is reorganized to present its key lemma and reasoning earlier.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main-text layout with revised typography and running headers, adds a first-page coverage figure, and enlarges and relabels retained experimental panels. The ridge and dense-ST figures move from the main text to Appendix M.

improvement.justification: v2 improves exposition and code-access information and adds direct coverage evidence and mathematical detail. However, it upgrades v1's empirical Lasso conclusion to a theorem whose Appendix J.2 proof has a substantive gap: its O(n^-1) approximation error can dominate the Ω(n^-5/4) lower bound on sqrt(gamma) it seeks to preserve. Because this gap affects a central new theoretical contribution, the useful additions do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
